policy: Entries waive one package + one GHSA advisory id each. A new advisory on an allowlisted package is NOT inherited and fails the gate. build-dev-toolchain entries are accepted without an expiry only while the vulnerable code never ships; runtime-accepted-debt entries MUST carry a rationale, an expiry, and a tracked follow-up in .agent/KNOWN_ISSUES.md, and are the explicit escalation path when no compatible fix exists. Never silently waived.

allowlist.rationale: ICNS parser infinite loop reached only while Metro parses images on the developer/CI machine; the vulnerable code never ships in the app bundle (no runtime import path). Tracked in .agent/DEPENDENCY_AUDIT.md.
JXL/HEIF parser infinite loops with the same Metro-only reachability as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr; build-time image parsing only, not embedded in the shipped binary.

v3/v5/v6 buffer-bounds advisory for uuid < 11.1.1 reached only through xcode -> @expo/config-plugins -> Expo CLI/prebuild/config toolchain. The vulnerable call pattern (explicit buf argument) is not exercised by first-party code or the toolchain; not runtime-bundled.

ReDoS (exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input, CWE-400/405/407) reached at runtime via expo-router@57 -> query-string@7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component. Impact is a crafted deep-link query string hanging the JS thread. Campaign 053 re-evaluated the officially compatible remediation envelope: expo-router@57.0.22 (current SDK 57 line, latest 57.x) pins query-string ^7.1.3, and every query-string 7.x release pins decode-uri-component ^0.2.2, so no patch within the supported line can carry the fix; query-string@9.x would supply the patched decode-uri-component@^0.5.0 but 0.5.0 is `"type": "module"` (ESM-only) while expo-router requires query-string from CommonJS (`__importStar(require("query-string"))` in build/getPathFromState.js), so forcing it would break route parsing at runtime; npm audit's only offered fix remains an expo-router semver-major downgrade to 5.1.11, which is out of scope and would regress SDK 57. App-owned route parameters are additionally bounded by `apps/mobile/src/routing/route-params.ts`, which is defense in depth only and does NOT remediate this upstream decoder advisory. Follow-up: drop this entry when expo-router advances to a query-string major that carries the fix (next planned Expo SDK upgrade); tracked in .agent/KNOWN_ISSUES.md.
